key_insight: Among four WC-10Co-4Cr spray processes, HVOF and HVAF produced the best overall wear performance, while HVAF delivered the strongest corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that thermal spray process selection strongly controls carbide coating hardness, tribology, and corrosion behavior on stainless steel parts.
method: WC-10Co-4Cr coatings deposited on 304 stainless steel by APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, wear rate, friction coefficient, and electrochemical corrosion response
Linked performance differences to coating density, carbide load-bearing behavior, and wear mechanism evolution
evidence_signal: Hardness increased from 771.4 HV (APS) to about 1166 HV (HVOF/HVAF), wear rate dropped to 1.10–1.17×10^-5 mm3/N·m for HVOF/HVAF, and HVAF showed the best corrosion metrics (Ecorr −0.37 VSCE, Icorr 1.75 μA/cm²).
watch_item: The results are specific to 304 stainless steel substrates and the tested spray parameters, so coating rankings may shift with process tuning or different service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
